newsitem.title: USA: NASD finalizes rule on mutual fund sales at banks.
newsitem.headline: NASD finalizes rule on mutual fund sales at banks.

text.p: The National Association of Securities Dealers said it approved final rules intended to reduce customer confusion when purchasing uninsured financial products like mutual funds at banks.
Several surveys have shown widespread customer confusion about the applicability of federal deposit insurance to ordinary mutual funds sold at banks.
NASD officials said in a conference call with reporters Wednesday that the final rule would now be submitted to the Securities and Exchange Commission for approval.
Last March, the SEC issued the NASD's preliminary proposal for comment. The final rules were revised to take into account many of the comments, NASD officials said Wednesday.

Three of the most controversial portions of the preliminary proposal were removed from the final rules, officials said. Instead of being forwarded to the SEC, the NASD issued for comment revisions of those three portions, covering risk disclosure, sharing of confidential customer data and a prohibition on referral fees.
Rules in the three revisions issued for comment would apply to all transactions instead of just sales in banks.
The preliminary rules, including the three portions now left out, applied only to actions by broker-dealers on the premises of banks, NASD officials said.

NASD's action follows a policy issued in 1994 by U.S. bank regulators governing bank actions when selling uninsured investment products like mutual funds. While the bank regulators' policy governs all banks, NASD rules govern actions by broker-dealers affiliated with banks.
Many banks have set up broker-dealer units and others have established joint marketing arrangements with independent broker-dealers.
The banking industry had sharply criticized the preliminary rules, but bank officials seemed pleased with the revisions in the final rules.

"It's just been a tremendous step forward," said Sarah Miller, senior government relations counsel for the American Bankers Association, based on a general outline of the final rules. "But we'll have to see how the proposal really looks and the details," she added.
The ABA wants the rules to apply equally to a bank's own broker-dealer unit or to an outside broker-dealer selling products in a bank with a joint marketing agreement, she said.

Under the final rules, banks should, whenever possible, sell uninsured products in a separate location in the bank from the place where retail deposits are taken, NASD officials said. If that is not practical, the bank would be required to post signs or notices indicating the distinctions between the two types of transactions.
The NASD tried "in every instance possible to make this rule as consistent with the (bank regulators' rules) as we can," an NASD official said.
